name: COBOL
title: COBOL (ISO/IEC 1989:2023)

type.text: **Typing is weak and static**: A `PICTURE` clause fixes an item's shape, but a `MOVE` between items with different pictures converts the value silently, so the declared type does not protect it
**The Data Division declares the shape once**: Level numbers and `PICTURE` state each item's size and category, and the Procedure Division uses that declaration without repeating it
**Group items give a structured record**: Level numbers nest elementary items inside groups, so a record layout is one declaration
**Fixed decimal arithmetic is exact**: `COMP-3` packed-decimal operations do not accumulate binary floating-point error, so the numeric representation matches monetary values
**`USAGE` decides the representation**: `COMP-3` (packed decimal), `COMP` (binary), and `DISPLAY` differ, and a move between them converts without a type error
**An alphanumeric item accepts any character string**: An `X(n)` item holds any text, so a category mistake is caught only by the program's own checks

construction.text: **Every data item is visible to every paragraph**: A `WORKING-STORAGE` item can be read and modified from any procedure, and before COBOL-85 the language offered no way to restrict access to it
**The four divisions separate concerns**: Identification, Environment, Data, and Procedure give each declaration a fixed place, so data definition does not share a space with program logic
**`CALL ... USING` passes parameters to a subprogram**: A called program receives its arguments explicitly, so a subprogram boundary is a declared interface
**`LOCAL-STORAGE` gives per-call state**: It is allocated for each invocation, so a re-entrant call does not share the state held in `WORKING-STORAGE`

**`PERFORM THRU` names a range of paragraphs and passes nothing**: The called region is a text span and the performed code communicates only through shared data items, with no parameter list and no call stack
**`GO TO` and `ALTER` break structured flow**: The language permits control transfers that obscure which paragraph runs next

memory.text: **Ordinary program data needs no allocator**: `WORKING-STORAGE` and `LOCAL-STORAGE` come from a declared layout, so a program that uses only them calls no allocator and no free
**No garbage collector**: Storage is fixed at compile time, so reclamation is deterministic and unobserved
**`OCCURS` declares fixed-size tables**: The size of a table is known at compile time
**`OCCURS DEPENDING ON` varies a table's length at run time**: The logic then couples to the actual occurrence count
**`ALLOCATE` and `FREE` put deallocation back on the programmer**: The 2002 standard added dynamic allocation for tables and objects, and release is an explicit statement

error.text: **Error handling has no structured path**: `USE AFTER STANDARD ERROR` and other declaratives are declared globally in the `DECLARATIVES` section, and control may or may not return to the failing statement
**The declaratives section is separated from the main procedure**: Recovery code is declared apart from the normal path
**`FILE STATUS` reports I/O results as data**: A file's `FILE STATUS` item holds a two-character code that the program can test after each I/O statement
**`INVALID KEY` and `AT END` put the failure case at the statement**: `READ ... INVALID KEY ... NOT INVALID KEY` and `AT END` handle the result inside the operation itself
**An error need not terminate the program**: A declarative can return control after a failure, so a caller cannot rely on termination
**No value carries the failure**: There is no exception object and no result type, so detail travels only through shared items

concurrency.text: **Concurrency belongs to the transaction monitor**: `EXEC CICS` and IMS link a program to a transaction environment instead of a language thread model
**Batch steps are single-threaded by design**: A batch program runs to completion without shared-memory concurrency
**The 2023 standard defines asynchronous messaging**: ISO/IEC 1989:2023 adds asynchronous message handling and transaction processing, so a program need not hand-roll that loop
**The language has no threads or synchronisation primitives**: Any parallel work couples the program to the monitor
**Shared `WORKING-STORAGE` across transactions needs external discipline**: A pseudo-conversational program must reset its state between transactions

platform.text: **A large share of production runs on IBM mainframes**: Much COBOL executes on z/OS with IBM compilers, so practice is largely one vendor's
**The language is an ISO standard**: ISO/IEC 1989:2023 is the current edition, so the language is not owned by a single vendor
**GnuCOBOL is an independent compiler**: It is an open-source project separate from GCC and translates COBOL to C
**Vendor extensions bind a program to a compiler**: `EXEC CICS`, `EXEC SQL`, and vendor libraries do not compile unchanged elsewhere
**Newer standard features are unevenly implemented**: The 2002 object-oriented features and the 2023 additions are not uniformly available across compilers

performance.text: **Compiled ahead of time to native code**: IBM Enterprise COBOL and GnuCOBOL (through generated C) produce machine code, so no interpreter and no JIT warm-up sits on the path
**`USAGE` selects the representation per item**: `COMP-3` packs two digits per byte where compact storage matters
**A batch step amortises start-up over millions of records**: One run processes the whole job
**Tuning is platform-specific**: IBM's optimiser and GnuCOBOL produce different code, so a tuned program does not transfer unchanged
**Exact decimal arithmetic is slower than binary**: `COMP-3` operations cost more than native binary arithmetic

ecosystem.text: **The ecosystem is legacy and vendor-fragmented**: IBM, Micro Focus, and GnuCOBOL each supply their own compiler, runtime, and tooling
**The mainframe tooling is proprietary**: The compilers, monitors, and debuggers are commercial products
**GnuCOBOL is open source and maintained**: It gives the language a free compiler
**A long-lived body of documentation exists**: The ISO standard and the vendor manuals are complete and stable over decades
**The deployed base is enormous**: Gartner reported over 200 billion lines of COBOL in 1997, and the language remains among the most widely deployed
**The skills base is shrinking**: Retirements reduce the pool of maintainers, a risk exposed by the COVID-era unemployment-systems crisis

evolution.text: **The standard is backward compatible across decades**: COBOL-74, -85, 2002, 2014, and 2023 code coexist, and programs written decades ago still compile
**ISO/IEC 1989:2023 added modern features**: Asynchronous messaging, transaction processing, and dynamic-capacity tables join the language
**Revisions are infrequent**: A new standard edition arrives at intervals of a decade or more, so a needed feature waits a long time
**Adoption of a new feature is uneven**: A compiler may not implement a standard feature for years after publication

domain.text: **Strong lock-in to mainframe transaction and batch processing**: The language assumes fixed records, files, and a monitor runtime, so code carries that shape outside its home domain
**Superb for high-volume batch and transaction processing**: The fit to financial and administrative workloads is close
**Still runs the bulk of card-payment background processing**: The source reports COBOL behind most credit and debit-card swipe processing
**Fixed-point decimal arithmetic fits money**: The data model matches monetary computation without floating-point error
**Poor for nearly everything else**: Interactive, systems, and scientific work have little COBOL tooling

learning.text: **The learning curve is steep in practice**: Verbosity and over 300 reserved words must be learned
**The syntax is English-like**: `MOVE A TO B`, `ADD ... GIVING`, `IF ... END-IF`, and `DISPLAY` read close to prose
**The division structure is a fixed learning path**: Four divisions in a defined order give a predictable place for each declaration
**The vocabulary is large**: More than 300 reserved words, and each verb carries many optional clauses
**The tooling is not beginner-friendly**: Mainframe editors, JCL, and compile procedures are learned separately from the language

syntax.text: **Verbose**: Every statement names its verb and its operands, and paragraphs need explicit names
**English-like and self-describing**: The verb names the operation, so a statement is readable without symbol decoding
**`END-IF`, `END-PERFORM`, and `END-READ` bound a scope**: Explicit terminators remove the ambiguity of implicit scope
**Fixed-format column rules still shape style**: Column 7 is an indicator and the code sits in columns 8–72 in the classic reference format, and free format is an option
**The four-division prologue is long**: Even a minimal program declares Identification, Environment, Data, and Procedure

testing.text: **`FILE STATUS` and `INVALID KEY` give checkable I/O outcomes**: A test can assert on the status item after a file operation
**Compilers supply tracing and dump facilities**: IBM Debug Tool and GnuCOBOL's runtime tracing report execution, and `COB_SET_TRACE` enables a trace at run time
**GnuCOBOL runs on ordinary workstations**: The open-source compiler executes test jobs locally
**No test framework is in the language or the standard**: A harness is external, so a suite couples to the tooling
**A batch test needs representative data**: The job needs real files and JCL, not just a unit of code

security.text: **Fixed `PICTURE` sizes bound every item**: An oversized source value is truncated or padded on assignment rather than overrunning a buffer
**No pointers in the classic language**: A COBOL program cannot forge an address
**The transaction monitor authorises access**: CICS and RACF check a transaction's resource use
**Truncation is silent**: A value that does not fit an item is truncated without an error, so data can be lost quietly
**Dynamic SQL is injectable unless host variables are used**: `EXEC SQL` with host variables is parameterised, but a statement built from a string re-opens SQL injection

tradeoffs: **The small standard library is a scope decision**: The standard specifies 43 statements, 87 functions, and one class, and adds no general-purpose library beyond them
**The fixed reference format comes from the punched card**: Columns 1–6 hold a sequence number and column 7 an indicator, and free format is now permitted, so the old constraint is optional
**Mainframe batch orientation is a scope decision**: COBOL assumes file and transaction processing in a monitor, which suits high-volume work and excludes systems programming
**The `PICTURE`-driven fixed record suits flat files**: The declared layout matches a fixed-length record, which is a modelling choice for the domain
**The installed base is a business constraint**: Retaining legacy programs is an organisational decision, not a property of the language
verdict: COBOL's two scores are deliberately even: its own constructs impose about as much coupling as its platform and ecosystem do. The four divisions and the `PICTURE` clause declare a record once, `CALL ... USING` gives a subprogram an explicit parameter interface, and `LOCAL-STORAGE` gives per-call state, but the default visibility of every data item to every paragraph, the paragraph-range semantics of `PERFORM THRU`, and error handling by declaratives that may not terminate the program make global coupling the norm. The platform side is legacy, vendor-fragmented, and locked to mainframe transaction processing, with a shrinking skills base. Inside high-volume batch and transaction processing COBOL is excellent; outside that niche the fit is poor.

energy.text: Compiles to native code: the fastest class in the language energy and time benchmarks [@pereira2017energy; @pereira2021ranking]. A causal re-analysis attributes the difference to execution time [@vankempen2025green].

ai-readiness.text: Sparse training data: models write it unreliably [@joel2025lowresource].

safety.text: No certified or standards-qualified path for safety-critical systems.
